questions.question: What is the safest first branch point for a patient with reproductive potential who has pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding?
choices: Assume the cause is a routine menstrual change
Assess hemodynamic stability and pregnancy possibility early
Begin hormonal therapy before evaluation
Schedule screening only
questions.explanation: Pelvic pain or bleeding requires early assessment of stability and pregnancy status. Positive pregnancy with pain/bleeding can represent ectopic pregnancy or another urgent complication.

questions.question: Which pattern most strongly supports emergency ectopic-pregnancy evaluation?
choices: Stable chronic mild dysmenorrhea without pregnancy possibility
Positive pregnancy test with unilateral pelvic pain, dizziness/syncope, shoulder pain, or hypotension
A normal routine cervical screening result last year
Mild vaginal itch without pain
questions.explanation: Pregnancy plus pain/bleeding with severe pain, shoulder pain, weakness, dizziness/syncope, or instability can indicate rupture/internal bleeding and requires emergency care.

questions.question: What is the appropriate approach to a pelvic examination?
choices: Perform it for every patient regardless of preference
Use ongoing informed consent, privacy, explanation, appropriate equipment/competence, and respect a patient’s choice to pause or decline
Skip history because the examination supplies all information
Force completion if the diagnosis is uncertain
questions.explanation: A pelvic examination is consent-based and not required for every complaint. If it cannot be done safely or is declined, use an alternative diagnostic/referral pathway.

questions.question: Which presentation requires urgent evaluation rather than routine outpatient management of abnormal uterine bleeding?
choices: Mild stable spotting without anemia symptoms
Heavy bleeding with hypotension, tachycardia, syncope, severe weakness, or evidence of major blood loss
A recorded normal menstrual cycle
One resolved episode of minor spotting after a known benign cause
questions.explanation: Acute heavy bleeding with signs of hypovolemia or major anemia needs stabilization and emergency evaluation before a longer etiologic workup.

questions.question: Why should vaginal discharge or dysuria not be treated repeatedly as yeast infection or UTI without reassessment?
choices: Symptoms always diagnose an STI
Cervicitis, PID, dermatitis, genital lesions, urinary disease, and other causes can overlap
Testing is never useful
All symptoms require hospitalization
questions.explanation: Vaginal and urinary symptoms overlap across infectious and noninfectious conditions. Site-appropriate testing, pregnancy status, and examination guide safer care.

questions.question: Which finding supports a PID-focused assessment in an at-risk patient with lower-abdominal/pelvic pain?
choices: Only a normal blood pressure
Cervical motion tenderness, uterine tenderness, or adnexal tenderness in the appropriate clinical context
A remote history of seasonal allergies
An unchanged mole
questions.explanation: PID can be clinically subtle. Pelvic/lower-abdominal pain with cervical motion, uterine, or adnexal tenderness warrants consideration alongside pregnancy-related and surgical alternatives.

questions.question: What is the best role of pelvic ultrasound in suspected ectopic pregnancy?
choices: It replaces emergency disposition in an unstable patient
It can help evaluate pregnancy location and pelvic structure within an appropriate emergency/obstetric pathway
It proves every pregnancy is intrauterine regardless of timing
It is required before a pregnancy test
questions.explanation: Ultrasound is a targeted diagnostic tool. Instability or suspected rupture requires emergency care; imaging does not replace stabilization and disposition.

questions.question: Which statement about ectopic-pregnancy risk is most accurate?
choices: Only patients with known risk factors can have ectopic pregnancy
Prior ectopic/PID/tubal factors can increase risk, but ectopic pregnancy can occur without recognized risk factors
Contraception makes pregnancy impossible
A recent period excludes ectopic pregnancy
questions.explanation: Risk factors help but do not exclude disease. Evaluate pregnancy status and symptoms rather than relying on a risk-factor checklist.

questions.question: Which symptom pattern should prompt timely diagnostic follow-up rather than reassurance based on prior normal screening?
choices: Persistent unexplained abnormal/postcoital bleeding or a new concerning pelvic mass/symptom pattern
A healed minor skin scratch
Stable asymptomatic contraception use
One day of mild self-limited menstrual cramping
questions.explanation: Prior screening does not explain a current concerning symptom. Persistent abnormal bleeding, new masses, or other warning patterns require appropriate diagnostic evaluation.

questions.question: What is essential in a safe outpatient women’s-health plan?
choices: Avoid discussing return precautions
Document pregnancy assessment, testing/referral ownership, access barriers, and specific emergency precautions for worsening pain, bleeding, fainting, fever, vomiting, or instability
Assume all pelvic pain has a gynecologic cause
Use medication alone without follow-up
questions.explanation: Pelvic and bleeding complaints can evolve. Clear safety netting, closed-loop results/referrals, and access-aware follow-up protect against delayed diagnosis.
